questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have always been fascinated by Italy and the Italian culture so for me it was a personal preference already from the beginning. But I knew also that Bologna had the oldest university in the world and that, I think, was a clearly upside because the university was big and culturally important as well. 
Furthermore I found it appealing that Bologna isn't that big of a city - I wanted to get to know the city I was supposed to live in and find my own way of living there and that was a easier achieved if the city wasn't to big.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There wasn't so much information upon arrival - I attended an online meeting with people from UNIBO and that was good but I still had a lot of questions regarding deadlines for a lot of things that turned out to be without any concerns but when everything is new and you have to fit into a new system it would be helpful to have even more information to stick to. But UNIBO was great at helping out when you yourself reached out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not enough.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There is a lot of information and things to deal with during the mobility and especially when you have arrived. You have to choose your courses after your arrival and that can be a little stressful but don't worry, you have time to change the courses almost through the whole exchange period. The leaning agreement can be signed again, so I would recommend to get it resigned when you are completely sure of the courses but of course before you return to Denmark - the Erasmus Grant cannot be granted to you if you don't have the learning agreement signed before your return to Denmark.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not easy. Bologna is a huge student city so a lot of people are staying on exchange both domestic and foreign students, so there is a lot of pressure on the housing solutions.
My recommendation is to start searching as soon as you can on Facebook pages for Erasmus students in Bologna or at different housing sites online, but be careful of scams. I had a good experience with Housing Anywhere.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a lovely city and has a lot of great areas except the area around the train station. It is nice to live within the city walls because a lot of campuses are placed in the city center but there are many nice places outside of the walls as well so don't be scared of booking that - you have to get used to walk long distances either way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for a second round spot and it was very easy to send the application. The only thing that would have been appreciative for was a little bit more structure and information from the point when I got accepted. There were information letters that the students from first round received that I didn't but had to ask for information myself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both the administration on KU and the KU-UCPH abroad have been nice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful. I even got registred for a class that normally has student limit from a specific course of education - I didn't knew this limit when I registred but UNIBO told be and said that I was welcome to ask the administration for a spot in the class and I got that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a little difficult to get a overview of the many different classes. Be aware of the location because UNIBO has many location also far outside of Bologna. Then the next thing is to type down the different class schedules so you make sure that the classes don't overlap. I experienced that they changed the time schedule after having registred to the classes but then you just make a new study  plan on your personal unibody site and change your learning agreement. Therefore I would recommend to get the final learning agreement signed when you are certain in your classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 5 classes at 6 ECTS points each. Some classes matched this amount of points but some classes were way more time-consuming than 6 points I think.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the classes I had was quit similar in teaching style. I study art history in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Italian Cinema
Italian Culture
Exhibition, New Media and Performance Art
Art Law in a Digital Age
Feminist Critique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You can live quite cheap but you eat out a lot so in the end it would be the same amount of costs as in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot activities that you register to but for the sports you need a medical certificate with you from your doctor in Denmark, so if you want to do sport on Campus make sure you bring that to Bologna. You can read about it on UNIBO's website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join the trips myself but I know a lot of people who attended the different trips and excursions for the incoming exchange students - if I was supposed to go again I would attend at least a couple of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around the city and look up on all the beautiful buildings, go visit the many nice museums and galleries, do aperativo and go for a run in Giardina Marguerit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out for an aperativo or just chat with the locals in class. Be open-minded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language - I took a language course before arrival which turned out to be a good solution.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything! Their leaned back way of living, the art, the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Structure your mobility period before and after arrival so you have a good overview on the deadlines and information you need to provide. After that enjoy and do yourself the favor of going on train trips around the different parts of Italy. The country has so much to offer and then you hopefully feel the great feeling when you return to Bologna - this city is amazing and that you realize when you compare it with other Italian cities. It made me appreciate Bologna even more and made me feel at home in the city as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the culture, the academic classes. I'm very satisfied.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
